printers.intro: Connect PlateGuard to the systems in your restaurant: the kitchen printer and the till.
printers.title: Kitchen printer
printers.how: Every allergy order prints a ticket with the checklist on the kitchen's own printer, so the kitchen works without a screen. Works with Star printers that support CloudPRNT (TSP100IV, mC-Print3 and others).
printers.none: No printer yet. Allergy tickets show on the kitchen screen only.
printers.name: Printer name
printers.waiting: {count, plural, one {# ticket waiting} other {# tickets waiting}}
printers.tested: Test page sent. It prints the next time the printer checks in, within a few seconds.
printers.addressTitle: Enter this address in the printer
printers.step1: Open the printer's settings page in a browser (its IP address is on the self-test print).
printers.step2: Under CloudPRNT, turn CloudPRNT on and paste this address as the server URL. Set polling to 5 seconds.
printers.step3: Save, restart the printer, then press Test print here.
printers.once: This address is shown once. Lost it? Ask for a new address: the old one stops working.

pos.title: Till
pos.how: Orders rung up in the till become plates on the seats in PlateGuard, judged against the guest's allergies, and an allergy ticket goes to the kitchen next to the till's own ticket. Allergies come from the waiter in PlateGuard, or straight from the till: a button such as "Allergy: milk" or a note such as "no nuts". Put the seat in the till too ("Seat 2"), as a button or in the line's note.
pos.noSecretKey: The server has no key to store the till's secrets encrypted yet. Add the environment variable INTEGRATION_SECRET_KEY in Vercel (a long random text) and deploy again.
pos.webhookStep1: In the Square Developer Dashboard, open Webhooks → Subscriptions, make sure Sandbox is selected, and press Add subscription.
pos.webhookStep2: Paste the URL below as the notification URL and tick the events order.created and order.updated. Save.
pos.webhookStep3: Open the subscription, copy its Signature key and paste it here.
pos.webhookOther: The webhook was set up with another address: {url}. Save the signature key again to use this one.
pos.webhookWaiting: Webhook set up. Nothing received yet: place a test order below.
pos.itemsTitle: Link the till's items to dishes
pos.itemsHow: Each item in Square stands for one dish. The test account starts empty: put the published menu in it with one press.
pos.noItems: No items from the till yet.
pos.testHow: Rings up an order in the Square test account the way a till would, with the table and the seats. PlateGuard takes it in at once; the webhook then brings the same order again, without doubling it.
pos.linkFirst: Link at least one item to a dish first.

pos.buttonsHow: When the waiter taps a button such as "Allergy: milk", or types "no nuts" on a line, PlateGuard puts that allergy on the seat and judges the plate with it. PlateGuard reads most names by itself; set a button by hand when the name says something else.
pos.buttonsNone: The till has no buttons or modifiers yet.
pos.webhookElsewhere: The webhook and the log of what came in are under Webhooks.

connectHow.square: In the Square Developer Dashboard, open your application, switch to Sandbox and copy the Sandbox access token under Credentials, and the test location's ID under Locations. The token is stored encrypted and never shown again.
connectHow.lightspeed-k: Lightspeed sends no messages by itself: PlateGuard fetches the open checks. Paste an access token of the Lightspeed API (scope orders-api) and the business location ID. Until PlateGuard is a Lightspeed partner, use the demo account Lightspeed gives you.
connectHow.mplus: MplusKASSA sends every order to PlateGuard by itself. Connect here first; then set up the webhook in Mplus with the address PlateGuard shows you.

pos.liveAccount: This is the live restaurant account, not the demo account
pos.itemsHowLive: Each item in the till stands for one dish. Items appear here once they have been rung up.
pos.noWebhooks: This till sends no messages by itself. PlateGuard fetches its open checks: use "Fetch open orders" below.
pos.mplusStep1: In MplusKASSA, open Beheer > Instellingen > Webhooks and add a subscription.
pos.mplusStep2: Paste the URL below as the endpoint URL, give a subscription ID, and tick at least addSessionLine, updateSessionLine and completeSession.
pos.mplusStep3: Make up a secret key (Base64), enter it in Mplus and paste the same key here.

incidents.title: Incidents
incidents.intro: Allergy incidents reported by staff. What was known at that moment is frozen with each report; the guest data of that visit is kept for the follow-up.
incidents.reportHow: What happened? The plate, its checks and who did what are saved with the report as they are now.
incidents.sent: Incident reported. A manager follows it up.
incidents.followUpHow: Write down the cause and the measure taken so it does not happen again. Closing needs both.
incidents.noAllergies: No allergies were recorded for this seat.
incidents.noPlate: The report is not about one plate.
incidents.noChecks: No checks were recorded for this plate.
incidents.noTimeline: No steps were recorded for this seat or plate.

start.title: Get started

start.step2Open: {count, plural, one {# point left to check.} other {# points left to check.}}
start.step3Text: Guests and staff only see the published version.

start.nextText: Want the waiter to record allergies per seat, the kitchen to get an allergy ticket and the cook to scan the plate? Add that when you are ready, with a link to your POS too.

webhooks.none: No till is linked yet. Link one under Integrations first; its webhook then shows here.
